primary_spec.natural_language_summary: Keep the input’s exact 7-bar chord progression and key center, and re-orchestrate into a lo-fi chill texture: Rhodes electric piano as the lead, upright bass, and a lo-fi brushed kit. Use straight 8th groove and drop2 voicings with moderate texture density (0.45). Creative suggestion: keep harmony supportive to the groove (don’t over-emphasize extended colors beyond what the given chord qualities already imply).

alternative_spec.natural_language_summary: Preserve the input’s exact 7-bar chord progression, but shift the feel toward a more hip-hop lo-fi character: swung 16ths, spread voicings with 9ths, and slightly lighter texture density (0.42). Use Rhodes electric piano lead, upright bass, lo-fi brushed kit percussion, plus vinyl-crackle ambience. Creative suggestion: apply the style’s extended-color mindset (maj7/maj9/min7/min11/sus-like smoothness) only as compatible with the given chord qualities, without changing the bar-by-bar chord identities.

divergence_points.rationale: Validator disagreement: tradition favored straight 8ths to avoid changing groove identity too aggressively, while style favored swung 16ths as more typical for lo-fi chill. Both are allowed style enums.

Validator disagreement: tradition chose drop2 as a safer, more supportive voicing; style chose spread-with-9ths to better realize extended-color harmony. Both voicing styles are in the allowed enum set.

Minor disagreement from the debate: both are within the style’s moderate density range; primary keeps the slightly higher density that tradition proposed, while alternative follows the style translator’s lighter 0.42.
Style translator included vinyl crackle; tradition omitted ambient. Since no dynamics/articulation evidence is provided, this divergence is treated as an optional timbral layer.

Both specs resolve the hard constraint noted in the debate: input tempo is 60.0, so tempo must remain within ±20%. The debate proposals used 72/84 and were flagged; both synthesized specs set tempo to 60 to satisfy the constraint.
